children: Russia’s S&P Global Manufacturing PMI declined to 48.8 in August from July’s six-month high of 50.7, marking the first contraction in the sector in three months.
The contraction was driven by decreases in production and new orders, while employment and stock levels contracted further.
Output shrank for the first time since April, albeit at a marginal pace, linked to lower new orders.
The modest decrease in new orders was due to weak client demand and reduced liquidity among customers.

Firms recorded a renewed fall in input buying, with stocks of purchases and finished goods both falling at faster rates, while supplier delivery times lengthened the most since December 2024 due to logistics issues and fuel shortages.
On the price front, both input and output cost inflation accelerated to a seven-month high, due to higher fuel and imported goods prices.
Looking ahead, business sentiment improved amid hopes of strengthening demand conditions and increased investment in advertising.

title: Russia Manufacturing Returns to Contraction
